extracted.intended_audience: sponsors/applicants seeking FDA approval of new drugs (NDA/ANDA/505(b)(2)), regulatory affairs professionals, and attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and substantive standards for preparing, submitting, and justifying New Drug Applications (NDAs), Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs), and certain 505(b)(2) submissions to FDA under 21 CFR Part 314, including accelerated and animal-rule pathways and postapproval obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Part 314
rubrics_metrics.description: This part sets forth procedures and requirements for the submission to, and the review by, the Food and Drug Administration of applications and abbreviated applications to market a new drug under section 505 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, as well as amendments, supplements, and postmarketing reports to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exclusions (e.g., products licensed under the Public Health Service Act and certain provisions not applying to designated medical gases) and that references to CFR are to chapter I of title 21 unless noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — approval based on safety and effectiveness and surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose is to establish an efficient and thorough drug review process to (a) facilitate the approval of drugs shown to be safe and effective and (b) ensure the disapproval of drugs not shown to be safe and effective; and to establish an effective system for FDA's surveillance of marketed drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations should be construed in light of these objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include reports and all pertinent information
rubrics_metrics.description: An NDA is required to contain reports of all investigations of the drug product sponsored by the applicant, and all other information about the drug pertinent to an evaluation of the NDA that is received or otherwise obtained by the applicant from any source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative duty to submit adverse information, new analyses, and other newly acquired information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and types of copies required
rubrics_metrics.description: Three copies of the NDA are required: an archival copy, a review copy, and a field copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An NDA for a new chemical entity will generally contain an application form, index, summary, technical sections, case report tabulations, case report forms, drug samples, and labeling. Other NDAs will contain items needed for their particular submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit a completed and signed application form containing: applicant name/address; date of NDA; NDA number if previously issued; drug product names (established, proprietary, code, chemical); dosage form and strength; route of administration; identification numbers of referenced INDs, drug master files and other applications; proposed indications for use; statement of submission type (original, 505(b)(2), resubmission, supplement); prescription vs OTC marketing proposal; checklist of enclosures; signature requirements (and US-resident countersignature if signer not in US).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature may be by applicant or authorized official; if signer not resident in US, countersignature by US-resident attorney/agent/official required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archival index requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The archival copy of the NDA is required to contain a comprehensive index by volume number and page number to the summary, the technical sections, and the supporting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index must allow reviewers to locate supporting materials efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary requirement (content and editorial standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: An NDA must contain a summary in enough detail that the reader may gain a good general understanding of the data and information in the NDA, including quantitative aspects. The summary should synthesize information into a well-structured and unified document and be written at approximately the level of detail required for publication in refereed scientific and medical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data should be presented in tabular and graphic forms where possible; FDA may use the summary for the public Summary Basis of Approval. The summary must include proposed labeling text (with annotations to supporting summary/technical sections), pharmacologic class and rationale, marketing history outside US, CMC summary, nonclinical tox/pharmacology summary, human PK/bioavailability summary, microbiology summary (anti-infectives), clinical data and statistical analyses, and a concluding benefit-risk discussion including proposed postmarketing studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical sections required and sufficiency standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA must contain technical sections with data and information in sufficient detail to permit the agency to make a knowledgeable judgment about whether to approve the NDA or whether grounds exist to refuse approval under section 505(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists required technical sections (e.g., Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls; nonclinical; clinical) and emphasizes sufficiency of detail for regulatory judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) — drug substance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The CMC section must include a full description of the drug substance: physical/chemical characteristics and stability; name and address of manufacturer; method of synthesis/isolation and purification; process controls used during manufacture and packaging; and specifications necessary to ensure identity, strength, quality, purity, and bioavailability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives may be proposed to meet requirements; reference to current USP/NF may satisfy relevant requirements; include tests, analytical procedures, and acceptance criteria (stability, sterility, particle size, crystalline form, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: CMC — drug product requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a list of all components used to manufacture the drug product and statement of composition; specifications for each component; name/address of each manufacturer; description of manufacturing and packaging procedures and in-process controls; specifications to ensure identity, strength, quality, purity, potency, and bioavailability (e.g., sterility, dissolution rate, container closure); and stability data with proposed expiration dating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives (components, procedures, controls, analytical procedures) may be submitted; USP/NF citations may satisfy some requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batch production and testing records for study lots
rubrics_metrics.description: For each batch used to conduct a bioavailability/bioequivalence study or used in a primary stability study, provide the batch production record; specifications for components and product; names/addresses of sources of active and noncompendial inactive components and container/closure systems; names/addresses of each contract facility and identification of operations performed; and results of tests required by applicable cGMP regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures traceability of clinical/stability lots to production and testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master production record requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the proposed or actual master production record, including a description of the equipment to be used for manufacture of a commercial lot or a comparably detailed description of the production process for a representative batch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports reproducible commercial manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA must contain either a claim for categorical exclusion under 40 CFR §§25.30 or 25.31 or an environmental assessment under 40 CFR §25.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with NEPA-related environmental documentation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and labeling linkage requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA summary must include the proposed text of the labeling, including any Medication Guide, with annotations to the summary and technical sections that support each labeling statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If NDA is for a prescription drug, statements describing reasons for omitting labeling sections per §201.57 must be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate and well-controlled studies as evidentiary standard
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA approval decisions rely on adequate and well-controlled studies demonstrating effectiveness (and safety) except where specifically authorized alternate pathways apply (e.g., accelerated approval or animal-rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to 'adequate and well-controlled' recur throughout; when alternate endpoints or evidence are used, postmarketing verification and additional controls are often required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated approval based on surrogate or non-mortality clinical endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may grant marketing approval on the basis of adequate and well-controlled clinical trials establishing an effect on a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit or on a clinical endpoint other than survival or irreversible morbidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval under §314.510 is subject to the requirement that the applicant study the drug further to verify and describe its clinical benefit when uncertainty exists; postmarketing studies must be adequate, well-controlled, and conducted with due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval with restrictions to assure safe use (postmarketing restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA concludes a drug shown effective can be safely used only if distribution or use is restricted, FDA will require postmarketing restrictions needed to assure safe use, such as distribution limited to certain facilities or physicians with special training or conditioning distribution on performance of specified medical procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations will be commensurate with the specific safety concerns presented by the drug product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal procedures for accelerated approval
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may withdraw approval (after hearing) for drugs approved under accelerated pathways if postmarketing studies fail to verify clinical benefit; applicant fails to perform required postmarketing study with due diligence; postmarketing use shows restrictions inadequate; applicant fails to adhere to restrictions; promotional materials are false/misleading; or other evidence shows drug not safe/effective under conditions of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure includes notice of opportunity for hearing, timelines for requesting a hearing (15 days) and submission of hearing data (30 days), publication of notice of hearing in Federal Register when timely requested, and modified separation-of-functions rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postmarketing safety reporting and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Drug products approved under accelerated or other subparts are subject to the postmarketing recordkeeping and safety reporting requirements applicable to all approved drug products as provided in §§314.80 and 314.81.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must comply with adverse event reporting, periodic reports, and any additional postmarketing commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of promotional materials for review
rubrics_metrics.description: For drugs considered under accelerated or animal-rule pathways, applicants must submit copies of all promotional materials (labeling and advertisements) intended for dissemination within 120 days following marketing approval during preapproval review; after 120 days submit promotional materials at least 30 days prior to initial dissemination unless otherwise informed by agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps FDA assess promotional claims for compliance; failure to comply may be grounds for regulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of postapproval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA determines after approval that requirements (postmarketing studies, restrictions, promotional submissions) are no longer necessary for safe and effective use, it will notify the applicant and ordinarily remove such requirements when verification of benefit or appropriate labeling demonstrates safety and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may also remove requirements upon review of sponsor petitions under §10.30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal rule (approval when human efficacy studies unethical or infeasible) — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to certain new drug products for which definitive human efficacy studies cannot be conducted because it would be unethical to deliberately expose humans to a lethal or permanently disabling toxic biological, chemical, radiological, or nuclear substance and field trials have not been feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not apply to products approvable under other FDA efficacy standards like accelerated approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal rule — evidentiary criteria for reliance on animal studies
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may grant marketing approval based on adequate and well-controlled animal studies when results establish the drug is reasonably likely to produce clinical benefit in humans only when: (1) there is a reasonably well-understood pathophysiological mechanism of toxicity and its prevention/substantial reduction by the product; (2) effect demonstrated in more than one animal species expected to predict human response (unless a single species is sufficiently well-characterized); (3) the animal study endpoint is clearly related to the desired human benefit (generally enhancement of survival or prevention of major morbidity); and (4) data on kinetics/pharmacodynamics in animals and humans allow selection of an effective human dose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval is contingent on these four conditions being met and FDA may consider other available data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal rule — postapproval obligations and safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Approvals under the animal-rule are subject to: (1) required postmarketing studies (when feasible and ethical) to verify and describe clinical benefit and assess safety, conducted with due diligence when feasible; (2) approval with restrictions to ensure safe use (restricted distribution, conditioning on medical procedures, recordkeeping); and (3) patient labeling that explains approval was based on animal studies and provides indication(s), directions, contraindications, foreseeable risks, adverse reactions, anticipated benefits, drug interactions, and other relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patient labeling must be available with the product prior to administration/dispensing when possible; applicants must include a plan for such postmarketing commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal rule — withdrawal and hearing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may withdraw approvals granted under the animal-rule if postmarketing studies fail to verify benefit, applicant fails to perform required studies with due diligence, postmarketing experience shows restrictions inadequate, applicant fails to adhere to restrictions, promotional materials are false/misleading, or other evidence shows product not safe/effective; procedures include notice of opportunity for hearing, timelines for requests and data submission, and publication of hearing notices if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation of functions will not apply in these withdrawal proceedings; advisory committees will participate as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete response letter defined
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete response letter is a written communication to an applicant from FDA usually describing all of the deficiencies that the Agency has identified in an NDA or ANDA that must be satisfactorily addressed before it can be approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A resubmission following a complete response letter is governed by class 1 vs class 2 distinctions based on the nature of the information provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 1 and Class 2 resubmission definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 1 resubmission: resubmission following a complete response letter containing items such as final printed labeling, certain safety updates, stability updates, commitments to postmarketing studies, assay validation data, final release testing, minor reanalyses, and other comparatively minor information. Class 2 resubmission: any resubmission that includes items not specified as Class 1, including those requiring presentation to an advisory committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines review timeframes and procedural handling of resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and standards related to bioavailability/bioequivalence/specifications/strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Bioavailability: rate and extent to which active ingredient is absorbed and becomes available at site of action; Bioequivalence: absence of significant difference in rate and extent between products when administered at same molar dose under similar conditions in appropriately designed study (with caveats for intentional rate differences in modified-release forms); Bioequivalence requirement: FDA-imposed requirement for in vitro/in vivo testing that must be satisfied as a condition of marketing; Specification: quality standard (tests, analytical procedures, acceptance criteria) provided in an approved NDA/ANDA to confirm quality of materials; Strength: amount of drug substance in a dosage unit or container.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions specify how FDA will assess equivalence and quality; bioequivalence may be assessed by scientifically valid measurements for non-systemically absorbed products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV certification / paragraph IV acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph IV certification is a patent certification of invalidity, unenforceability, or noninfringement described in the specified sections for NDAs and ANDAs; a paragraph IV acknowledgment letter indicates FDA has determined a 505(b)(2) application or ANDA with paragraph IV is sufficiently complete to permit substantive review and is regarded as filed/received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers patent-notice and litigation timelines and has implications for exclusivity (e.g., 180-day exclusivity definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: 180-day exclusivity period definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The 180-day exclusivity period begins on the date of the first commercial marketing of the drug by any first applicant and ends the day before an ANDA submitted by an applicant other than a first applicant could be approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines timing for generic entry related to paragraph IV certification and first applicant status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tentative approval defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Tentative approval is notification that an NDA or ANDA otherwise meets approval requirements but cannot be approved because of exclusivity or court-ordered date restrictions; a tentatively approved drug is not an approved drug and will not be approved until FDA issues an approval letter after necessary review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers situations such as orphan, pediatric, and other statutory exclusivities or court orders under patent litigation.
